text:
Alex: quick thread — proposing a split in the onboarding pipeline: a tight SLA-oriented "fast slab" that verifies latency/throughput and runtime compatibility, and a separate "validation slab" that runs deeper quality/regression checks asynchronously. tradeoffs below.
Priya: sounds reasonable. can you sketch what each slab would assert?
Alex: fast slab checks: model loads with expected KV cache behavior, <200ms p95 on our ci-small GPU profile, correct tokenization (no unknown tokens), and binary-level ABI pass. low-cost, small sample. validation slab: sampling across golden prompts + end-to-end quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-based evals), distributional checks, quantization tolerance matrix. runs on dedicated workers, results feed back to rollout gating.
Jamie: nit: how do we avoid false negatives in the fast slab? mini samples can be flaky.
Marco: we should allow the fast slab to be permissive for quality but strict for runtime invariants. e.g., fail if memory growth > X% or if kernel mismatch is detected. quality failures should be advisory until validation slab confirms.
Priya: agree. also want an explicit contract for sample selection. fast slab uses 5 short canonical prompts + tokenizer smoke; validation slab uses 500 stratified prompts across seqlen buckets.
Sasha: cost concern: running full validation for every model will blow our budgets. propose a heuristic: run full validation on new model-major versions or if any fast-slab runtime anomaly occurs; otherwise run a lightweight delta-eval compared to latest vetted model.
Alex: good point. add rollout triggers: full validation if (a) quantization level changed, (b) model arch changed, (c) fast slab reports runtime divergence. delta-eval otherwise.
Jamie: how will this appear in Console? I want clear per-model status: FAST_OK / VALIDATION_IN_PROGRESS / VALIDATION_FAIL. Need API hooks for product teams to block rollouts when VALIDATION_FAIL.
Marco: we can reuse existing rollout policy primitives. Add two new signals: fast_slab_signal and validation_signal. Rollout policy uses them with configurable strictness: e.g., prod tenants default block on validation_fail, dev tenants can ignore.
Priya: who owns telemetry for these signals? If no owner, alerts will be noise.
Sasha: proposed owners: eng-ml owns fast_slab infra and runtime metrics; product-ops owns validation metrics and golden-set curation. Both teams share SLOs.
Alex: action items: 1) define fast slab asserts and thresholds (Sasha + Marco), 2) spec validation sampling strategy + delta-eval (Priya + Jamie), 3) Console signal wiring + rollout policy mapping (Marco), 4) cost/runbook for when validation backlog grows (eng-ml + infra).
onboard-bot: created intake ticket #ONB-1627 for "validation-slab: sampling spec & rollout mapping" (assignee: Priya).
Jamie: I can draft sampling strata tomorrow. will include seqlen, genre, and prompt temperature variations.
Sasha: one more: we should capture model fingerprint (architecture, tokenizer hash, quant bits) in the intake so fast slab can do deterministic ABI checks. small schema example: 
```
intake:
  model_hash: abc123
  tokenizer_hash: def456
  quant_level: int8
  architecture: llama2-7b
```
Alex: thanks — that fingerprint will also help cache-compat checks for KV layout.
Priya: marking this as RFC-followup. i'll consolidate into a short PRD and link ONB-1627. :+1:
Marco: SG. tagging in eng-sre for potential infra quotas impact. :thinking:
Sasha: quick thumbs: :thumbsup: if you agree with the split and action items.
Alex: thanks all, closing thread for now.
